This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is by the claimant for enhancement of compensation passed in MVC No.1257/2015 by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT-Sedam (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for short) dated 23.08.2019.
2. With consent of both the side, the matter is taken up for final disposal, though it is slated for admission.
3. The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for sake of convenience.

It is the case of the claimant that on 29.04.2015 around 8:00 p.m., near Jakanapalli Tanda Cross,
petitioner had sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of tractor and trailer bearing Reg.No.KA- 32/T-7431-7432 by its driver.
As a result of this, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
He had taken treatment by spending more than R.3,00,000/-.
He was an agriculturist and earning Rs.12,000/- per month and also doing business and earning Rs.4,00,000/- per annum.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, he has been suffering from permanent disability.
With these reasons, prayed to award the compensation.
5. The respondent Nos.1 and 2 denied the contents of the claim petition and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Tribunal had framed the necessary issues.
The claimant to prove his case examined PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 18.

The Gourishankar vs Hanumanth And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124233944/
2
respondents have not led any evidence.

8. The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record,
assessed age of claimant as 29 years, notional income Rs.7,000/- per month, disability 25%,
multiplier 17 and on that basis had awarded the following amount of compensation:-
Sl.No. Heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs.20,000=00 2.
Attendant charges, food and Rs.1,500=00  conveyance charges
3. Loss of future income Rs.3,57,000=00 4.
Medical expenditure Rs.1,88,000=00 5. Loss of income during Rs.14,000=00  treatment 6. Loss of amenities and nutrition Rs.20,000=00  food  Total Rs.6,00,500=00 9.
Heard the arguments of learned counsels for both side.
10. The learned counsel for the claimant submits that income and disability assessed by the Tribunal is NC: 2024:KHC-K:4919 incorrect.

As per the contentions of the claimant who is earning more than Rs.4,00,000/- per annum by agricultural as well as business, but the Tribunal has taken income at Rs.7,000/- per month, which is on the lower side.
He further submits that the amount of compensation awarded under other heads is also meager.
Therefore prayed to enhance the same.
11. The learned counsel for the respondent - insurer supported the impugned judgment and submitted that there are no reasons to interfere in the findings of the Tribunal in the impugned judgment.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
2. The following question arises for determination.
"Whether the claimant is entitled for the enhancement of compensation?
12. Considering the impugned judgment, the amount of compensation awarded under other heads except medical expenses needs to be reconsidered.
The claimant had sustained fracture of right humerus, fracture of third metatarsal bone and crush injuries to the right wrist.
He was admitted as inpatient for three days from 18.01.2017 to 21.01.2017.
He is an agriculturist, fracture of the right hummer and other fracture i.e. crush injuries to right wrist definitely affect his earning capacity.

Gourishankar vs Hanumanth And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124233944/
3 14.
There is no material to prove the income; if he was earning Rs.4,00,000/- per annum from the business he could have filed income tax receipts and ought to have produced income tax return.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has taken notional income as Rs.7,000/- per month, which is on the lower side.
If we consider the chart prepared by the KSLSA, notional income could be taken as Rs.8,000/- per month.
There is no dispute regarding the age and multiplier and respondent-insurer has not filed any appeal against the impugned judgment.

Therefore, as accepted by the Tribunal permanent disability taken by the Tribunal as 25% to the whole body.
Considering the NC: 2024:KHC-K:4919 materials on record, compensation needs to be reassessed and following amount of compensation is awarded under different heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 01. Pain and suffering Rs.30,000/-

02 . Medical expenses Rs.1,88,000/-
 03. Special Diet, Attendant charges, etc., Rs.20,000/-
 04. Loss of future earning capacity due to Rs.4,08,000/-
 permanent disability  (8,000x12x17x25%)
 05. Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-
 06. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.24,000/-
 (8,000 x 3 )
 Total Rs.7,00,000/-
Awarded by the Tribunal Rs.6,05,000/-

The amount of enhancement Rs.99,500/-
15.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation of Rs.99,500/-
along with interest on the said amount at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. It is not in dispute that the respondent - insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

For the above said discussion, I answer above question partly in the affirmative and pass the following;
 ORDER  i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
iii. The respondent - insurance company shall deposit the said amount with interest within a period of 06 weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
The entire enhanced amount of compensation is ordered to be released in favour of the claimant after due identification.
v. The registry is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
